confidence: high for the code chain; device reproduction still required for the final KVO-fires-on-pushState step
user_consequence: A signed-in super-admin account (production has exactly one: admin@helmsportslabs.com) that signs in on the native app is bounced back to the golf login screen instead of reaching the Helm Bridge admin console, and reproducing it (sign in again) reproduces the same bounce -- a de-facto login loop for that account on native. Separately, any Baseball invite link (/baseball/join/<code>), which the app deliberately generates and shares outside the app, dumps the recipient at golf login instead of the baseball join page if GolfHelm is the only Helm app installed on their phone.
mechanism: GolfBridgeViewController.swift's URL observer (lines 82-96) classifies every WKWebView URL change with substring checks: isGolfPage = url.contains("/golf/"); isAboutPage = url.contains("/about")||contains("/privacy")||contains("/terms"); if neither, it calls onNavigateAway, which SceneDelegate.swift (lines 20-29) wires to a hard webView.load() of https://www.helmsportslabs.com/golf/login. This allowlist has no entry for /admin or /baseball/*, both of which are real, deliberately-reachable same-origin destinations. (1) admin path: src/lib/golf/admin-redirect.ts:31-34 resolves the super-admin's post-login destination to the literal string '/admin' (ADMIN_CONSOLE_PATH). src/lib/utils/safe-redirect.ts:12-28 explicitly allowlists '/admin' as a safe internal redirect target alongside /golf/ and /baseball/ prefixes, specifically so the login/welcome/signup/reset flows can honor it. src/components/auth/golf-sign-in-form.tsx routes the admin account through '/golf/welcome?next=%2Fadmin' (safe, contains /golf/), then src/app/golf/(auth)/welcome/page.tsx sets destRef.current to that next value (or recomputes it via resolveAdminPostLoginPath at line 235 when next is absent) and, after its ~3s greeting, calls router.replace(destRef.current) at line 326 -- a same-document Next.js client navigation to '/admin'. WKWebView updates its .url property (and fires KVO) for same-document History API navigations, so the classifier sees '/admin', misclassifies it as leaving golf, and immediately overwrites the WebView with /golf/login. The same admin-redirect helper is also called from src/components/NativeRedirect.tsx:52-58, documented in admin-redirect.ts's own header as the 'native cold-start bounce' path (mounted on the marketing root page, src/app/page.tsx:36). (2) baseball manifestation: public/.well-known/apple-app-site-association registers BOTH '/golf/*' and '/baseball/*' universal-link path patterns under GolfHelm's sole iOS App ID (ios/App/App/App.entitlements declares only one associated-domain app, MK49MSX29G.com.helmsportslabs.golfhelm). src/components/baseball/command-center/BaseballInviteButton.tsx:42 builds real, shared invite links at '/baseball/join/<code>'. Tapping such a link on a device where GolfHelm is the only Helm app registered for helmsportslabs.com hands the Universal Link to GolfHelm's WKWebView; the resulting same-origin, allowlisted (capacitor.config.ts:25 allowNavigation includes helmsportslabs.com) URL still fails the classifier's substring test and triggers the same login bounce.
expected: A valid, deliberately-reachable same-origin destination (an allowlisted admin surface, a shared baseball invite) never becomes a login detour, per this lane's own proof bar.
actual: The native URL classifier's allowlist is a fixed 4-substring OR-list ('/golf/', '/about', '/privacy', '/terms') that does not know about '/admin' or '/baseball/', even though the web app's own redirect-safety allowlist (safe-redirect.ts) and the AASA universal-link config both treat those paths as first-class.
proposed_fix: Replace the substring OR-list with an explicit, exact-match allowlist owned in one place (ideally sourced from or mirroring the same prefixes safe-redirect.ts already encodes: /golf/, /baseball/, /admin, plus the legal pages), parsed via URLComponents (path/host), not raw substring .contains. Treat unmatched-but-same-host paths as 'stay' by default and only bounce on an actual different host or the real marketing/product chooser paths this was built to catch.

confidence: high - mechanism fully traceable in source, no device needed to establish it fires; physical perception needs hardware
user_consequence: A single logical outcome (e.g. a failed 'Delete account' action) produces a tap-acknowledgment haptic plus two full error-notification haptics back to back, and a successful save produces a success haptic twice. Every screen that pairs a Fairway Button with an explicit outcome haptic and a fairwayToast call double- or triple-buzzes for one event, contradicting this lane's own stated grammar ('a button, handler and success toast cannot independently vibrate for the same event').
mechanism: Three independent, uncoordinated haptic emitters exist for the same user action: (1) src/components/fairway/controls/button.tsx:163-172 wraps every non-asChild Button's onClick and unconditionally fires fwHaptic('light') before calling the consumer's own onClick; (2) many handlers explicitly call triggerHaptic('success'|'error'|...) themselves inside that onClick, e.g. src/components/fairway/pages/settings/FairwaySettingsGeneral.tsx:585-599 and :1554-1557 and :1665-1673, and src/components/fairway/pages/team/FairwayTeamSettings.tsx:185-260 (repeated pattern, 6+ call sites in that one file); (3) src/components/fairway/feedback/ToastStack.tsx:145-151 makes fairwayToast.success/warning/danger/error() independently call fwHaptic('success'|'warning'|'error') every time a toast of that kind is shown -- and the handlers above call one of those fairwayToast methods right after their own triggerHaptic call on the same result. None of the three call sites checks whether another one already fired for this action.
expected: One haptic owner per logical operation outcome (per this lane's own mission and plan section 9.4).
actual: Up to three haptics fire for one outcome: the Button's auto-tap 'light', the handler's explicit success/error, and the toast helper's own success/error.
proposed_fix: Make fairwayToast the single owner of outcome haptics (it already has the semantic kind) and remove the ad hoc triggerHaptic('success'|'error'|...) calls immediately preceding a fairwayToast call of the matching kind; keep the Button's tap-in 'light' as the only pre-outcome haptic, since it precedes the async result rather than duplicating it.
owner_lane: A01 (haptic dispatch contract) with A03 (Button/toast consumers) and each feature lane for its own call sites

confidence: high for the code chain; device confirmation needed for the actual visible flash under real hardware and OS dark mode
user_consequence: A player or coach using the app's dark theme sees a light cream flash/rim at the native shell layer -- on cold launch before the first CSS paint, during elastic overscroll past the top or bottom of any scrollable screen, and at the splash-to-content handoff -- regardless of their chosen theme, because the native shell never learns the app is in dark mode. The launch screen and the WebView's own background are also two different colors, producing a visible color shift on every cold launch independent of theme.
mechanism: GolfBridgeViewController.swift:49-53 sets view.backgroundColor, webView.backgroundColor, and webView.scrollView.backgroundColor to a hardcoded UIColor(1.0, 254/255, 250/255) (#FFFEFA) once in viewDidLoad, with webView.isOpaque = false at line 51 so this color shows through any transparent moment. Nothing in the iOS project overrides traitCollectionDidChange or re-applies this color; ios/App/App/Info.plist has no UIUserInterfaceStyle key; the only theme-aware native call is src/lib/utils/capacitor.ts:190-194's syncStatusBarToTheme(), which updates ONLY the status bar glyph color (via CapacitorProvider.tsx's MutationObserver on <html class=dark>), never the view/webView backgrounds. Separately, the LaunchScreen storyboard (ios/App/App/Base.lproj/LaunchScreen.storyboard:25, rgb 0.929/0.878/0.784 = #EDE0C8) and capacitor.config.ts's SplashScreen.backgroundColor (#EDE0C8, line 82) are a distinctly different, deeper warm tan than the WKWebView's own #FFFEFA background -- the design-tokens.css author explicitly calls #FFFEFA 'cold, reads like white' in a comment at src/styles/design-tokens.css:288-290 explaining why the Liquid Glass tint was warmed away from it, yet the native shell still hardcodes exactly that color.
expected: Dark mode expresses the same depth with different luminance relationships in every layer, including the native shell -- no light-theme rims/flashes on dark surfaces (plan section 3, A03 boundary, applies equally to the native background that sits beneath every web paint).
actual: The native view/webView/scrollView background is a single hardcoded light cream with no dark variant and no update path, and it does not match the splash/launch-screen color either.
proposed_fix: Read the persisted theme preference (or OS trait) before the WebView first paints and set view/webView/scrollView.backgroundColor accordingly; add a JS->native bridge call (or a small native theme read of the same storage key CapacitorProvider/useGolfTheme uses) so a live in-app theme toggle updates the native background too. Align the splash/launch-screen color with whichever background the very next frame will show.

user_consequence: Rapid, repeated interactions that call triggerHaptic directly (the large majority of call sites) get no rate limiting at all, risking a continuous buzz/audible-click on older devices during fast repeated taps or drag-like interactions that were not routed through the semantic wrapper.
mechanism: src/lib/fairway/haptics.ts:119-128 implements a 32ms MIN_INTERVAL_MS throttle (shouldThrottle/lastFiredAt), but it is only consulted inside fwHaptic() (haptics.ts:131-140) and fwScrub().tick() (haptics.ts:183-187). A repo-wide count at this baseline finds 117 direct triggerHaptic(...) call sites outside haptics.ts/capacitor.ts versus 21 fwHaptic(...) call sites -- the majority path never touches lastFiredAt or shouldThrottle, so nothing limits its rate. (This also means the module header's claim of '164 of 177' call sites bypassing the preference gate is stale/inaccurate math at this baseline, though the underlying preference gate itself -- inside triggerHaptic, src/lib/utils/capacitor.ts:65-87 -- is correctly reached by every one of those 117 sites, since they all call triggerHaptic directly.)
expected: A single rate-limiting funnel that every haptic call site passes through, so rapid repeated triggers cannot produce a continuous buzz.
actual: The throttle only guards the minority (21 of 138) call sites that go through fwHaptic; the majority (117) direct triggerHaptic call sites are unthrottled.
proposed_fix: Move the throttle check into triggerHaptic itself (src/lib/utils/capacitor.ts) so every call site is covered, or migrate the remaining direct call sites onto fwHaptic over time; do not add a second throttle implementation.

confidence: high for the ordering claim; the actual wasted-fetch magnitude needs a device/network trace
user_consequence: Every cold launch forces a full network re-fetch of every JS bundle chunk, font, and image the app needs (HTTP disk+memory cache is wiped every time), adding avoidable latency to the exact moment (cold start) this lane's mission cares most about -- and the clear may not even be effective for the load it targets.
mechanism: GolfBridgeViewController.swift:22-28 calls super.viewDidLoad() (which starts Capacitor's own initial page load) BEFORE issuing WKWebsiteDataStore.default().removeData(ofTypes:[.diskCache,.memoryCache], modifiedSince:.distantPast), an async call with an empty completion handler and no ordering guarantee relative to the load super.viewDidLoad() already kicked off. The clear only removes WKWebsiteDataTypeDiskCache and WKWebsiteDataTypeMemoryCache -- it does not touch WKWebsiteDataTypeCookies, LocalStorage, IndexedDB, or ServiceWorkerRegistrations, so offline/durable app data (e.g. the round-sync outbox) is unaffected -- but it does happen on every cold launch (viewDidLoad fires once per scene-session root VC creation in SceneDelegate.swift:16-37; sceneWillEnterForeground/sceneDidBecomeActive at lines 75-84 are empty no-ops, so this is a once-per-cold-launch cost, not a per-foreground one).
expected: A targeted, version-aware cache policy that clears stale HTTP cache only when the deployed web release actually changed, without discarding a warm cache on every ordinary cold launch, and without racing the load it is meant to freshen.
actual: An unconditional disk+memory cache wipe on every cold launch, issued after the page load has already started, with no check of whether the deployed SHA changed since the last launch.
proposed_fix: Key the clear off a stored last-known release identifier (C01) compared against the current deployment; only clear when it changed, and do it before creating/loading the webView rather than after view lifecycle has already begun the load.

user_consequence: Repeatedly tapping the bottom-nav tab you are already on (a common real gesture, e.g. to scroll-to-top or just re-confirm) fires a selection haptic every single time, unlike the app's segmented control, which correctly produces none for a same-value reselect.
mechanism: src/components/fairway/app-shell/FairwayBottomNav.tsx:150-154 computes `active` (whether this tab matches the current route) for rendering aria-current, but the onClick at line 166 (`() => fwHaptic('selection')`) does not consult `active` before firing -- it fires unconditionally for every tap. By contrast, src/components/fairway/controls/segmented.tsx:303-308 relies on Radix ToggleGroup's single-select semantics, which do not invoke onValueChange (and therefore never reach fwHaptic('selection')) for a same-value reselect -- confirmed correct behavior for that control.
expected: A repeated tap on the already-selected control produces no haptic detent (plan section 9.4).
actual: FairwayBottomNav fires a selection haptic on every tap regardless of whether the tapped tab is already active.
proposed_fix: Guard the onClick with the already-computed `active` value: only call fwHaptic('selection') when `!active`.
owner_lane: A01 (haptic contract) / A02 (BottomNav ownership per plan section 3.3)

confidence: medium - the WebKit cross-origin download-attribute limitation is well-documented public behavior, but the exact runtime outcome inside this Capacitor bridge needs a device test
user_consequence: Tapping 'Download' on a coach/player document (PDF, image, or the PDFViewer/ImagePreview toolbar) does not reliably download the file in place inside the native app; depending on the runtime branch, it may silently do nothing, or hand off to the external Safari app for what the user expects to be an in-app action.
mechanism: src/app/golf/actions/documents.ts:1101-1104 generates a signed URL via supabase.storage.from('documents').createSignedUrl(path, 3600) WITHOUT the `{ download: true }` option, so the response carries no Content-Disposition: attachment header. src/components/golf/documents/DocumentPreview.tsx:127-134 (and equivalently ImagePreview.tsx:66-68, PDFViewer.tsx:63-65, FairwayRecruitDocuments.tsx:167-169) then builds a synthetic <a href={that cross-origin signed URL} download>.click(), relying on the HTML `download` attribute -- which WebKit does not honor for cross-origin resources, a well-documented WebKit limitation. The signed URL's host (the Supabase project's storage domain) is also not in capacitor.config.ts:25's allowNavigation allowlist (only *.helmsportslabs.com/helmsportslabs.com), so Capacitor's own documented navigation policy hands any such navigation to the external browser rather than the WebView -- meaning the practical outcome depends on whether a `download`-attribute click is even treated as the kind of navigation Capacitor's WKNavigationDelegate intercepts, which is not determinable from source alone. Two sibling components in the same codebase already implement this correctly: src/components/golf/documents/TextPreview.tsx:130-134 and src/components/fairway/pages/documents/FairwayDocuments.tsx:673-679 fetch the resource and download it via a same-origin blob: URL (URL.createObjectURL), which the `download` attribute does honor.
expected: A Download action reliably downloads the file inside the native app, the way TextPreview.tsx and FairwayDocuments.tsx already do.
actual: Four call sites build a download anchor pointed directly at a cross-origin signed URL with no Content-Disposition:attachment, a pattern that does not reliably trigger a download in WebKit.
proposed_fix: Reuse the existing fetch->blob->createObjectURL pattern from TextPreview.tsx/FairwayDocuments.tsx in the four broken call sites (reuse before replacement, per plan operating rules), or add `{ download: true }` to the createSignedUrl call so the server sends the attachment header.
owner_lane: shared change requested - documents feature owner (not A01); A01 supplies the native allowNavigation/bridge diagnosis

confidence: high for the mechanism; no live call site currently exercises the risky window under real interruption
user_consequence: If a sequenced haptic pattern's triggering action is interrupted (screen unmounts, app backgrounds, user rapidly navigates away) within the sequence's delay window, the later beat(s) still fire as a native call with no owner left to receive them -- a late, contextless pulse.
mechanism: src/lib/fairway/haptics.ts:143-157 (fwHapticSequence) schedules delayed beats via plain window.setTimeout with no returned cancel handle and no AbortSignal; nothing calls clearTimeout if the underlying action is interrupted. The only live product call site at this baseline is 'commit' from src/components/auth/golf-sign-in-form.tsx:145 (90ms second beat), immediately followed by a client-side navigation roughly 100ms later (line ~152) -- a narrow but non-zero race. PullToRefresh.tsx's two 'threshold' call sites use only a 0ms single beat, so they carry no risk. 'reject' and 'celebrate' sequences (110ms and 70/130ms delays) are defined in SEQUENCES but have no live product caller at this baseline -- only the dev/demo haptics page (src/app/golf/(dashboard)/dashboard/dev/haptics/page.tsx) invokes them.
expected: A cancelled/interrupted gesture produces no late haptic pulse (plan section 9.4).
actual: Sequence beats scheduled via setTimeout have no cancellation path; the only live risk window (golf-sign-in-form.tsx) is narrow (90ms vs ~100ms to navigation) but unguarded.
proposed_fix: Return a cancel() handle from fwHapticSequence that clears any pending timeouts; call it from an unmount/interruption path where a sequence's trigger action can be interrupted.

confidence: high - confirmed against the installed @capacitor/keyboard@8.0.5 type definitions in node_modules, not just public docs
user_consequence: None directly -- these are dead config keys -- but they create false confidence for a future engineer debugging keyboard behavior, who may assume iOS has a native scroll-assist layer in play when it does not, and waste time looking for interference between a nonexistent native mechanism and the real JS-side one.
mechanism: capacitor.config.ts:64-67 sets `resize: 'ionic'`, `resizeOnFullScreen: true`, `scrollAssist: true`, `scrollPadding: true`. Verified against node_modules/@capacitor/keyboard/dist/esm/definitions.d.ts (the actually-installed v8.0.5 package) at this baseline: the KeyboardPlugin config interface declares only `resize`, `style`, `resizeOnFullScreen`, and `autoBackdropColor` -- `scrollAssist` and `scrollPadding` do not exist in this plugin version at all (likely leftover from an older Cordova/Ionic-keyboard-era config) and are silently ignored. `resizeOnFullScreen` is documented Android-only. `resize: 'ionic'` is real (KeyboardResize.Ionic exists in the enum) but only resizes an `ion-app` element per its own doc comment (definitions.d.ts:115-120), which this non-Ionic app does not have, so it also has no effect here -- confirmed both from the installed types and from Capacitor's public docs. The entire, correctly-functioning keyboard-avoidance mechanism for this app is the JS-side triad already in place: `--keyboard-height` + `body.keyboard-open` (CapacitorProvider.tsx:125-178, globals.css:392-424) plus targeted scrollIntoView, deliberately opted out of via `data-fw-keyboard-aware` on self-resizing surfaces (Sheet.tsx:203, ModalShell.tsx:306, AskSurface.tsx:132, CoachHelmDrawer.tsx:177, FairwayMessages.tsx:493), and covered by keyboard-inset.test.ts. This REFUTES the 'duplicate resize' framing of seed G09 at this baseline -- there is no duplicate; the JS compensation is the sole real mechanism.
expected: Configuration only contains keys the installed plugin actually reads.
actual: Two of four Keyboard plugin config keys (scrollAssist, scrollPadding) are inert no-ops in the installed @capacitor/keyboard@8.0.5; a third (resizeOnFullScreen) is Android-only and irrelevant to the iOS keyboard-avoidance question it sits next to.
proposed_fix: Remove scrollAssist/scrollPadding (or replace with a comment explaining they are historical no-ops if there is a reason to keep them for Android/older-plugin compat), and consider switching resize from the no-op 'ionic' value to 'none' or 'body' with an explicit comment, since 'ionic' currently reads as if it does something.
